title: Product Contract to Control Envelope Walking Skeleton
what: Make a confirmed Product Contract travel through the single acceptance seam and produce a minimal versioned Control Envelope without mutating the machine when the contract is invalid.
criteria: A valid minimal contract produces a run identity, stage tree, terminal status, observations, and evidence references through the acceptance seam.
An invalid or incomplete contract fails before installation, process launch, or filesystem mutation.
The initial Historical Failure Registry maps every known High or Extreme row to an owner and proof lane.

title: Runtime Discovery and Payload Verification Slice
what: Extend acceptance from the confirmed contract through runtime capability discovery and target-specific payload verification with explicit selection and rejection evidence.
criteria: Python 3.11 and 3.12 candidates are judged by required capabilities rather than the presence of base pip.
Target operating-system markers, native wheel compatibility, hashes, and archive members are verified before install.
All rejected runtime and payload candidates return stable structured reasons.

title: Transactional Install and Platform Path Slice
what: Install the minimal product through staging, promotion, final-path smoke, rollback, and idempotent reinstall while proving one inherited data-root contract.
criteria: A successful install launches only from the final location and retains a durable installation receipt.
Injected staging or promotion failure rolls back without claiming a completed install.
The platformdirs Component Spike records adopted or rejected evidence without weakening explicit Product Adapter overrides or child inheritance.

title: Service Lease and Lock Ownership Slice
what: Let an installed product start, report, stop, and release a loopback service only when ownership is proved, with distinct busy, permission, stale, and foreign-owner outcomes.
criteria: Service and lease operations are idempotent and never take over an unproved owner.
Contention, crash, permission, stale-owner, and exact-path fixtures preserve fail-closed behavior.
The portalocker and filelock bake-off selects at most one candidate or retains the proven lock atom with a decision receipt.

title: Process and Listener Ownership Slice
what: Expose deterministic process and listener identity evidence for service preflight, including child trees, executable identity, PID reuse, and access-denied behavior.
criteria: A foreign listener is reported without stopping or reclassifying it as the current product.
PID reuse and access-denied fixtures fail closed while preserving useful observations.
The psutil Component Spike records adopted or rejected evidence against the same external behavior.

title: Network and Codex Probe Slice
what: Resolve and probe a contract-faithful fake Codex process while returning separate network and transport stages that can later be replaced by Real Lab evidence.
criteria: Codex candidate identity, requested and resolved model or transport, launch outcome, stdout, stderr, and exit category are recorded separately.
Network failures distinguish route, DNS, proxy, TLS, certificate-revocation, and target-HTTP stages.
No CI fixture requires a real Codex login or secret.

title: Short-essay Happy-path Product Slice
what: Let a user submit short text through the minimal Flask page or API and receive one complete analysis, polish, and synthesis result with persisted state and artifacts.
criteria: The user-visible page and API drive the same workflow and terminal result.
Run, stage, and structured error state survives process boundaries in SQLite.
Input, analysis, polish, synthesis, manifest, and receipts form one inspectable Run Artifact Set.

title: Concurrent Polish and Partial Success Slice
what: Run two polish candidates concurrently and make synthesis obey explicit full-success, partial-success, and total-failure semantics.
criteria: Fixtures cover zero through four concurrent branches, cancellation, and timeout.
One failed candidate yields partial_success with visible failure evidence and a result from the survivor.
Two failed candidates fail the run, and Codex failures are never silently retried.

title: Artifact Diagnostics and Exact Cleanup Slice
what: Make every run independently inventoryable, diagnosable, and cleanable without losing failure evidence or affecting resources owned by another run.
criteria: Artifact names remain unique for duplicate human titles and manifests detect missing, changed, or moved outputs.
One sanitized diagnostic bundle identifies the first failed stage without publishing credentials or raw sensitive Codex internals.
Exact cleanup accepts only proved run ownership and negative fixtures leave unrelated processes and files unchanged.

title: Secure Hosted CI Matrix
what: Run the acceptance seam and Historical Failure Registry on the promised three operating systems and two Python versions through least-privilege public GitHub Actions.
criteria: Fast pull-request and push checks and a manual full matrix cover Ubuntu 24.04, Windows Server 2022, and macOS 15 arm64 with Python 3.11 and 3.12.
Actions use read-only ordinary permissions, no product secrets, full commit SHA pins, bounded timeouts, superseded-run cancellation, and no expensive schedule.
Success receipts and seven-day failure bundles are sanitized and remain distinct from Real Lab or Desktop proof.

title: Reproducible Candidate Core Release Candidate
what: Produce a reproducible pre-1.0 Candidate Core package candidate that a second product could identify and verify without claiming that Real Lab acceptance has passed.
criteria: The package candidate includes an immutable version, manifest, SHA-256 checksum, exact dependency identities, and third-party notices.
A clean consumer verifies and exercises the package through the same Conformance Suite.
Release evidence clearly states that Hosted CI is not Real Lab or Desktop acceptance.

title: Phase 1 Windows Real Lab Canary
what: Prove the short-essay product and Candidate Core against the actual Windows x64 Lab, installed runtime, real Codex environment, diagnostics, and cleanup boundary.
criteria: Install, doctor, real Codex short-essay E2E, artifacts, and diagnostics pass or return one evidence-backed blocker.
Ordinary failures preserve the evidence-bearing state rather than triggering automatic rollback.
Platform completion restores the exact recorded baseline and repeats acceptance once.

title: Phase 1 macOS Real Lab Canary
what: Prove the short-essay product and Candidate Core against the actual Apple Silicon macOS Lab with the same contract and evidence boundary as Windows.
criteria: Install, doctor, real Codex short-essay E2E, artifacts, and diagnostics pass or return one evidence-backed blocker.
Model, transport, child environment presence, service lifecycle, and executable permission are observable without silent fallback.
Platform completion restores the exact recorded baseline and repeats acceptance once.

title: Phase 1 Gate and Immutable Candidate Core Release
what: Name the authoritative Phase 1 evidence, publish the immutable Candidate Core release, and state exactly which later Desktop claims remain unproven.
criteria: Both Real Lab canaries and their repeated clean-baseline runs are linked to one gate verdict.
The immutable release artifacts match the tested package identity and checksums.
The verdict does not upgrade CLI or Lab evidence into Desktop E2E.

title: Sanitized Public Image Export and Phase 2 Repository Gate
what: Create a new-history sanitized export from the approved immutable Public Image revision and create the second public repository only after the export is proven safe.
criteria: Every exported source item is classified and hashed against an allowlist and denylist.
Protected Prompt Assets, repository history, agent instructions, prior workflows, operational evidence, generated artifacts, and local state are absent.
Any unclassified item or secret or prompt scan result blocks creation of the second public remote.

title: Public Image Contract Install and Service Slice
what: Make the sanitized Public Image product consume the immutable Candidate Core through its own confirmed Product Contract and Product Adapter.
criteria: The second product verifies the Candidate Core identity and checksum instead of copying Core implementation.
Install, port 3130 ownership preflight, service lifecycle, doctor, diagnostics, and exact cleanup use the shared Control Envelope.
No product-specific fork of a Candidate Core atom is introduced.

title: Synthetic XML to Image Workflow Slice
what: Run the sanitized Public Image product from non-sensitive content through minimal XML to one simple generated image while retaining the required stage contract.
criteria: Synthetic Prompt Fixtures preserve required roles, slots, and parseable result shapes without protected business methodology.
The workflow produces one verified image and a complete Run Artifact Set.
Timeout, terminal state, failure evidence, and cleanup obey the same Candidate Core semantics as Phase 1.

title: Phase 2 Windows Conformance and Real Lab Canary
what: Prove the Public Image Product Adapter and simplified workflow against the actual Windows x64 Lab using the same Candidate Core revision as Phase 1.
criteria: The shared Conformance Suite passes without a product-specific Core fork.
Real install, port ownership, doctor, simplified image generation, artifacts, diagnostics, cleanup, and clean-baseline repeat pass or return one evidence-backed blocker.
Requested and resolved Codex identity is explicit and no fallback is silent.

title: Phase 2 macOS Conformance and Real Lab Canary
what: Prove the Public Image Product Adapter and simplified workflow against the actual Apple Silicon macOS Lab using the same Candidate Core revision as Phase 1.
criteria: The shared Conformance Suite passes without a product-specific Core fork.
Real install, supported service lifecycle, doctor, simplified image generation, artifacts, diagnostics, cleanup, and clean-baseline repeat pass or return one evidence-backed blocker.
Desktop sandbox and executable identity observations remain distinct from product-side failures.

title: Two-product Candidate Core Gate
what: Establish that one immutable Candidate Core revision has the same control semantics across both products and both real target platforms.
criteria: Both Product Adapters pass their Conformance Suites and Real Lab gates against one Candidate Core identity.
Any shared change has a migration note and re-proves both adapters in the same gate.
The gate claims only a candidate method for the promised user-space Skill-backed application scope.

title: Adapter Scaffolding Skill Slice
what: Generate only Product Adapter, conformance-test, Hosted CI, and thin-Skill surfaces from a confirmed Product Contract while reusing the immutable Candidate Core.
criteria: Repository inspection produces a draft but generation stops until safety, success, ownership, cleanup, and secret semantics are confirmed.
Generated output never regenerates process, lock, runtime, install, ownership, receipt, or cleanup atoms.
An ephemeral third dummy contract passes schema, static, and conformance checks without creating a third product repository.

title: Windows Codex Desktop E2E
what: Use a new Windows Codex Desktop task to prove GitHub installation, runtime setup, restart usability, real simplified image generation, and visible artifact inspection.
criteria: The attempt ledger groups failures by category and permits at most five attempts for the same unresolved category; a sixth attempt is prohibited.
A passing verdict requires the actual Desktop task and user-visible artifact flow, not shell, Lab, sample, or screenshot substitution.
If the fifth same-category attempt remains unresolved, stop the Windows Desktop branch, preserve evidence, and make the downstream Windows recording ticket skipped by policy.

title: macOS Codex Desktop E2E
what: Use a new macOS Codex Desktop task to prove GitHub installation, runtime setup, restart usability, real simplified image generation, and visible artifact inspection.
criteria: The attempt ledger groups failures by category and permits at most five attempts for the same unresolved category; a sixth attempt is prohibited.
A passing verdict requires the actual Desktop task and user-visible artifact flow, not shell, Lab, sample, or screenshot substitution.
If the fifth same-category attempt remains unresolved, stop the macOS Desktop branch, preserve evidence, and make the downstream macOS recording ticket skipped by policy.

title: Windows Recording Proof
what: After Windows Desktop E2E passes, produce a validated Windows recording while keeping product and recording verdicts independent.
criteria: If Windows Desktop E2E is terminally blocked after five same-category attempts, this ticket is skipped without a recording attempt.
When eligible, a real shakedown precedes formal recording and the output is checked for file presence, duration, frames, and readback.
The same unresolved recording failure category receives at most five attempts; after the fifth failure the Windows branch stops with retained evidence and no sixth attempt.

title: macOS Recording Proof
what: After macOS Desktop E2E passes, produce a validated macOS recording while keeping product and recording verdicts independent.
criteria: If macOS Desktop E2E is terminally blocked after five same-category attempts, this ticket is skipped without a recording attempt.
When eligible, a real shakedown precedes formal recording and the output is checked for file presence, duration, frames, and readback.
The same unresolved recording failure category receives at most five attempts; after the fifth failure the macOS branch stops with retained evidence and no sixth attempt.

title: Final Bounded Verdict and Exact Cleanup
what: Name the final evidence authority, report each Desktop and recording branch as PASS, BLOCKED, or SKIPPED, restore exact platform baselines, and perform only ownership-bounded cleanup.
criteria: A policy skip or blocked terminal ticket is reported as such and never converted into inferred success.
The same unresolved finalization or cleanup failure category receives at most five attempts; the fifth unresolved attempt stops work and preserves evidence with no sixth attempt.
The final claim remains limited to the platforms and proof lanes that actually passed, and exact cleanup leaves unrelated state unchanged.
